# Performance and tracing

<!-- Generated by `bun tools/agents/rules.ts --write` from tools/agents/rules.ts, down to the end marker; edit the rules there. AGENTS.md carries each rule as one line. -->

## slow-is-p0-traced (rule 16)

Anything slow is a P0 until a span names it, and the trace comes before the speed fix. Every stretch
of worker time sits under a `tracing::info_span!(target: "blaze", ...)` that names the work: the
macro path for a proc-macro expansion, the package, version and target kind for a unit, the query
and key, the creator of a scope being waited on. Its own CPU time (`self_cpu_ns`) is filled, so a
DuckDB query over `<BLAZE_HOME>/v2/profile/*.spans.parquet` says which item took the time and
whether it was busy or waiting. A sampler stack or a guess from a log is a lead. The PR that makes
something faster quotes the before and after from those spans.

## incremental-first (rule 60)

What blaze is for is the time between an edit and its result, so that is what is measured, profiled
and fixed first: a no-op, a comment edit, a one-line body edit, the first edit after a cold build,
an edit in a fresh process with nothing warm (the normal case once no daemon stays), and the memory
held between edits (none outside a `watch` session), on real large workspaces
(`verify-on-real-projects`; paradigmxyz/reth and tempoxyz/tempo are the targets). When incremental
work and cold-build work compete for time, incremental wins, and a cold-build cost is accepted where
it buys a faster edit (work done once at build end so an edit need not redo it, records written so a
restart can read them). Cold builds are not ignored: every design keeps the door open to a fast cold
build (nothing that makes cold time worse than linear in the work, no structure that only an edit
can use), a cold build that fails or regresses badly is still a bug, and its numbers are still
recorded; but tuning cold time is not picked ahead of an open incremental item until the owner says
the priority has changed. Say which of the two a speed change is for, and quote the edit-loop
numbers with it.
